entities.summary:
The transition from Ming to Qing, which took place in China between 1616 and 1683, marked a significant turning point in world history. This dynastic change, led by the Manchu people, had far-reaching consequences that shaped the course of Chinese history and beyond.

The Ming dynasty, which had ruled China since the 14th century, was facing internal strife and external threats. In 1616, the Manchu people, led by Nurhaci, began a series of military campaigns against the Ming, eventually capturing the capital city of Beijing in 1644. The new Qing dynasty, established by the Manchu, would go on to rule China for nearly three centuries, leaving a lasting legacy in politics, culture, and society.

The transition from Ming to Qing had a profound impact on Chinese society, leading to the suppression of the Han Chinese, the imposition of Manchu culture, and the expansion of the Qing Empire. The Qing dynasty also played a significant role in global politics, including its involvement in the Great Game of 18th-century Asian geopolitics.

This transition also had a lasting impact on Chinese culture, including the development of Peking opera, Chinese cuisine, and traditional medicine.

This dynastic change was a significant factor in the global shift of power from the Ming to the Qing, marking the beginning of a new era in world history.
